answer: A reputation vault works like a shared meadow: every agent that wants to transact must first lock a stake in it, and the vault only releases the stake after a delay, so a sybil farmer who spawns thousands of fake identities has to fund each one and wait out the same delay. A cipher-signed history ties each stake to one verifiable key, so the cost of faking a thousand agents becomes a thousand real stakes, not one script run.
